name: 72pt
tagline: Pre-launch iPhone + Mac catalogue of free open-source typefaces
description: 72pt is an unreleased pair of apps from Kalypso: an iPhone app that lets you type your own words into a hand-picked catalogue of free, open-source typefaces from independent designers, and a Mac app that installs the ones you saved — one at a time or a whole collection — so they appear in Figma, Sketch, and any other design tool. As of this check the site is a single marketing page with a 'Notify me at launch' email capture and no App Store link, no font list, and no pricing. Aimed at designers who want to browse and audition indie type on a phone instead of a font-manager grid.
agent_guidance: Nothing here is usable by an agent yet — the site is a waitlist page with zero font data, no catalogue endpoint, and no download. Do not cite it as a font source; go to Google Fonts, Fontshare, or the specific foundry instead. Re-check after launch, at which point it is a human font-browsing app for macOS/iOS and still not a programmatic asset source.
why_it_matters: Worth a placeholder because indie open-source type discovery is genuinely underserved on mobile, but today it is a promise, not a product.
evidence: https://72pt.app (WebFetch returned 403; re-fetched with curl, HTTP 200, full rendered copy read from the HTML)

name: Inter
tagline: Open-source UI typeface: 9 weights, true italics, text and display optical sizes
description: Inter is Rasmus Andersson's open-source typeface designed for computer screens and user interfaces, and the de facto default sans for a large share of modern web and product UI. Version 4.1 ships 2,000+ glyphs covering 147 languages across 9 weights (Thin 100 to Black 900) with true drawn italics, plus two optical sizes — Text (tall x-height, ink traps, bridges for small sizes) and Display (cleaner, more delicate at large sizes). It is available as static files, as the InterVariable variable font with weight and optical-size axes, via the rsms.me CSS CDN, and as the inter-ui npm package, all under the SIL Open Font License 1.1.
agent_guidance: Default to Inter whenever a brief says 'clean modern SaaS UI' and no brand font is specified — it is the safest, most legible, most widely-rendered choice and costs nothing. Prefer InterVariable plus font-variation-settings for opsz over shipping 18 static files, and set the Display optical size only above roughly 32px. Note the repo has not been pushed since Nov 2024: v4.1 is finished and stable, not abandoned, but do not expect new weights; if you need a mono companion pair it with JetBrains Mono or Geist Mono rather than waiting for one.
why_it_matters: The reference open-source UI typeface of the last decade — nearly 20k GitHub stars and the font most product interfaces are unconsciously benchmarked against.

name: Geist
tagline: Vercel's OFL typeface trio: Sans, Mono, and five Pixel variants
description: Geist is the typeface family Vercel built with Basement Studio for developers and designers, following Swiss design principles of simplicity and speed. It ships three families — Geist Sans, Geist Mono, and Geist Pixel (Square, Circle, Grid, Triangle, and Line variants) — each in nine weights from Thin to Ultra Black, as static OTF, WOFF2, and variable files. Distribution is the `geist` npm package with ready-made Next.js imports (GeistSans, GeistMono, GeistPixel), Google Fonts (a partial glyph set with limited font-feature-settings), or a zip from GitHub releases; everything is SIL Open Font Licensed.
agent_guidance: In a Next.js app this is the lowest-friction quality font pairing available: `npm i geist`, then `import { GeistSans } from 'geist/font/sans'` and apply GeistSans.variable on <html> — next/font handles subsetting and zero-CLS swap for you. Use the npm package, not the Google Fonts version, if you need the full glyph set or OpenType features. Geist Mono is a strong default for code blocks and terminals; Geist Pixel is a display novelty, so keep it out of body copy and never use it for anything a screen reader or small viewport has to handle.
why_it_matters: The house font of the Vercel/Next.js aesthetic, and the one open typeface that arrives pre-wired into the framework most agent-built apps target.
notable_for: Sans + Mono + Pixel in one family

name: Untitled UI
tagline: Figma UI kit plus React Aria + Tailwind v4 component library with an MCP server
description: Untitled UI is a paired Figma design kit and React component library covering base controls, application UI, marketing sections, and whole page examples. The React side is MIT-licensed source code you own — installed with the `untitledui` CLI rather than imported as a dependency — built on React 19, React Aria v1.20 for accessibility, Tailwind CSS v4, and TypeScript. It also runs a hosted MCP server so coding agents can search components by natural language and pull in full page templates, and bundles the 4,688-icon Untitled UI Icons set. Free tiers exist for both Figma and React; PRO unlocks the 10k+ component Figma file, 420+ page examples, Figma variables, and the larger React catalogue.

pricing_detail: Figma FREE $0 (2k+ components, 350+ styles, 20+ page examples, 900+ icons). Figma PRO SOLO $129 (was $169), PRO STUDIO $399 (8 seats), PRO BUSINESS $999 (20 seats), PRO ENTERPRISE $2,499 (unlimited, SSO/SCIM). React FREE $0 (MIT, open source). React PRO SOLO $349 (was $499, 5k+ components, 250+ page examples), PRO STUDIO $999 (8 seats), PRO BUSINESS $2,499 (20 seats), PRO ENTERPRISE $8,999 (unlimited, private repo). All paid tiers are one-time with lifetime updates.
agent_guidance: Reach for this over shadcn/ui when the job is a whole marketing site or an authenticated app shell rather than a handful of primitives — it ships finished page examples, not just parts, and the free React tier is MIT source you own. Wire up its MCP server first (`claude mcp add --transport http untitledui https://www.untitledui.com/react/api/mcp`): search_components does semantic visual search and get_page_template_files installs a whole page in one call, which beats guessing component names. Two traps: it is React Aria, not Radix, so it will not compose cleanly inside a Radix/shadcn tree — pick one primitive layer per app — and the counts in the marketing copy mix Figma and React, so the biggest catalogues (10k+ components, 420+ page examples) are the paid Figma file, not the free code.
why_it_matters: The largest design-kit-plus-code system that treats agents as first-class consumers, with a real MCP server and semantic component search rather than a docs page to scrape.
notable_for: hosted MCP server with 7 agent tools

name: Untitled UI on GitHub
tagline: The MIT source repos behind Untitled UI: components, icons, and 3 starter kits
description: This is the GitHub organisation that publishes the open-source half of Untitled UI. Its main repo, untitleduico/react, holds the MIT-licensed React component source built on Tailwind CSS and React Aria (1,867 stars, pushed August 2026); untitleduico/icons holds the free Untitled UI Icons line set as SVG and React components. Alongside them sit three ready-to-clone starter kits — Next.js, Vite, and a StackBlitz-hosted Next.js variant — that scaffold a project with the design tokens, theming, and dark mode already wired. Use this org when you want to read or vendor the actual source rather than work through the docs site.

agent_guidance: Go here instead of the marketing site when you need to read real implementation source — how a React Aria component is composed, what a token name actually is, or how the starter kits configure Tailwind v4. Clone untitledui-nextjs-starter-kit for a greenfield Next.js app rather than running init inside an existing repo with a conflicting Tailwind config. Watch the icons repo license: it is NOASSERTION on GitHub, not clean MIT like the react repo, and only the ~1,100 line-style icons are free — the duocolor, duotone, and solid styles are paid, so do not assume the full 4,688-icon set is available from here.
why_it_matters: The auditable source of a system most people only meet as a Figma file, plus the three starter kits that make it a one-command project seed.

name: Kibo UI
tagline: shadcn registry of 41 hard components shadcn/ui does not ship, plus 28 blocks
description: Kibo UI is a custom shadcn/ui registry of composable, accessible components that fill the gaps in the base library — Gantt charts, Kanban boards, a rich-text editor, image cropping, contribution graphs, dropzones, QR codes, code sandboxes, and video reels among them. It is built on React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, and Lucide, installs with `npx kibo-ui add <name>` straight into your existing components directory, and is MIT-licensed and free forever. Beyond the 41 registry items it publishes 28 page-block families (hero, pricing, changelog, case study, roadmap, codebase) and 1,101 copy-ready patterns across 53 shadcn primitives.

agent_guidance: Reach for Kibo the moment a shadcn/ui project needs something shadcn does not ship — Gantt, Kanban, contribution graph, image crop, rich-text editor, code sandbox. It is the same Radix + Tailwind + CSS-variable foundation, so it drops into an existing shadcn components directory without a second primitive layer, unlike Untitled UI. Install by exact registry name from https://www.kibo-ui.com/r/registry.json (40 registry:ui items plus a typography registry:style) rather than guessing; and be aware the heavier items (gantt, editor, sandbox, kanban) pull real client-side dependencies and drag/drop state, so keep them out of server components and off critical first-paint paths.
why_it_matters: The best-scoped complement to shadcn/ui: it deliberately builds only the complex components everyone else stops short of, and stays installable through the same registry mechanism.
notable_for: Gantt, Kanban, and rich-text editor for shadcn
